items.q: The fiqh of dealings between people, such as buying and selling.
Interest or usury, forbidden in Islam.
The verse that says Allah has allowed trade and forbidden riba (meaning).
Selling in Arabic.
The surah that begins "Woe to those who give short measure" (meaning).
Wealth may not be taken unjustly, but through trade by this.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said the truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with these (paraphrased).
items.a: The Blessed Prophets (عليهم السلام), the truthful and the martyrs

items.q: Our Beloved Master ﷺ said whoever cheats us is not this (paraphrased).
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ found wet food hidden under dry food in a pile of this.
Writing down a debt is commanded in this verse.
A loan must be paid back in this.
Gambling, forbidden in Islam.
Hoarding food to push up prices.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said Allah has mercy on one who is easy-going when he buys, sells and asks for this.
A debtor in hardship should be given this.
Forgiving the debt of one in hardship is this.
A bribe in Arabic.
Wealth gained from what is forbidden.
A trust held for another.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ was known as al-Amin because He ﷺ kept this.
The six things named in the hadith of riba: gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates and this.
Selling gold for gold must be equal and this.
Riba of excess in exchange is called this.
Riba of delay is called this.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who takes riba, gives it, writes it down and these.
Buying with payment now and delivery later of a described good.
Ordering something to be made, like furniture.
Selling at cost plus a stated profit.
A partnership where one gives money and the other works.
A partnership where all give money.
Renting or hiring.
Something given as security for a debt.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ died while His ﷺ armour was pledged with a Jewish man for this.
A guarantee for another's debt.
Transferring a debt to another person.
Selling something one does not own is this.
Too much uncertainty in a contract.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ forbade selling fruit before this.
items.a: It is clearly ripe (safe from blight)

items.q: The right to cancel a sale while still in the meeting place.
The right to return goods found to have a hidden fault.
In the Hanafi school, khiyar al-majlis is this.
items.a: Not recognised (the sale is binding once agreed)

items.q: In the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools, khiyar al-majlis is this.
The right to cancel within an agreed time, up to three days in the Hanafi school.
The right to cancel after seeing goods bought unseen, in the Hanafi school.
In the Hanafi school, the 'illah (reason) of riba in the six items is this.
items.a: Measure (by volume or weight) with the same kind

items.q: In the Shafi'i school, the 'illah of riba in the four foods is this.
The 'illah of riba in gold and silver in the Shafi'i school.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said: if the kinds differ, sell as you like if it is this.
Selling a sa' of good dates for two of poor dates is this.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ advised selling the poor dates for money, then doing this.
items.a: Buying the good dates with the money

items.q: Two sales in one, forbidden by the hadith, are called this.
The trick sale where one sells on credit and buys back cheaper for cash.
In the Shafi'i school, bay' al-'inah is this.
In the Hanafi, Maliki and Hanbali schools, bay' al-'inah is this.
A contract for profit in mudarabah: losses are borne by this party.
The worker in mudarabah gets this.
items.a: An agreed share of the profit

items.q: Before prophethood, He ﷺ traded with Khadijah's wealth for a share of the profit.
The right of a neighbour or partner to buy first when land is sold.
In the Hanafi school, shuf'ah belongs to the partner and also to this person.
In the Shafi'i school, shuf'ah belongs only to this person.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ forbade a townsman from selling for this person.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ forbade going out to meet these before they reach the market.
Bidding up a price with no intention to buy.
Selling over another's sale.
Selling with a stone toss deciding the item.
Selling an unborn animal's young.
Selling a debt for a debt.
A sale with a stated price that may be cancelled if the buyer is cheated hugely.
A sale that is defective in the Hanafi school, not void.
A sale that is void with no effect.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said buyer and seller keep the choice as long as they have not done this (paraphrased).
The famous principle "Benefit goes with liability" (meaning).
The famous principle "No harm and no harming" (meaning).
The Hanafi code of the Ottoman state on dealings.
The Majallah was issued in these years.
The number of articles in the Majallah.
The first of the Majallah's maxims, "Matters are judged by their aims" (meaning).
The maxim "Custom is given authority" (meaning).
The maxim "Hardship brings ease" (meaning).
The maxim "Certainty is not removed by doubt" (meaning).
The Hanafi Ottoman scholar who led the committee that wrote the Majallah.
items.a: Ahmed Cevdet Pasha رحمة الله عليه

items.q: The Hanafi scholar 'Ali Haydar رحمة الله عليه wrote this commentary on the Majallah.
Taj al-Din al-Subki رحمة الله عليه, son of Taqi al-Din, wrote a book on legal maxims with this title.
Of the five great legal maxims, the one about harm.
The Companion who narrated "Do fresh dates lessen when they dry?" (meaning), on selling them for dry dates.
items.a: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The sale of fresh dates on the tree for dry dates, allowed in small amounts for the poor.
The limit for 'araya in the hadith.
Salam was allowed for a known measure, known weight and this.
The Companion who narrated that people of Madinah paid in advance for fruit for one or two years.
A hire contract (ijarah) on a person, as for a worker, is called this in the Hanafi school.
A worker hired for anyone, like a tailor, is called this.
In the Hanafi school, a common hire is this for goods lost without his fault, by Abu Hanifah.
The Companion who made common workers like tailors liable to protect people's goods.
items.a: Our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The partnership in which partners work with credit and reputation, not capital.
The partnership in which partners share their work, like two tailors.
In the Shafi'i school, the only valid partnership is this.
The full partnership with equal capital, work and liability, allowed by the Hanafis.
The Companion who gave wealth in mudarabah to 'Umar's sons in Iraq, in a famous report.
The Companion of whom our Beloved Master ﷺ said "Allah bless you in your dealings" after he bought a sheep for one dinar and sold for two.
In the Hanafi school, salam requires this many conditions, including a known term and place.
